note: VM executes OP_TAILCALL; ra points to the callable slot on the Lua stack, b is the argument count plus the function slot.
The value at ra is not a function, so luaD_tryfuncTM is invoked to fetch the __call metamethod; each iteration increments b, growing the argument count.
luaD_tryfuncTM is entered to resolve the __call metamethod for the non-function value at func.
checkstackGC is called to guarantee stack space for the metamethod; if the stack is already at its limit this raises a stack overflow error via luaG_runerror.

code: luaD_pretailcall (lua_State *L, CallInfo *ci, StkId func, int narg1)
note: After the metamethod loop, luaD_pretailcall is invoked to prepare the tail-call frame for the resolved Lua closure.
checkstackGC requests stack space for the tail-call frame; the requested size exceeds the remaining stack capacity, triggering a stack overflow error.
luaG_runerror raises the stack overflow error; while formatting the error message it reads beyond the heap-allocated stack buffer, causing the heap-buffer-overflow READ.
